answer: Agents resist Sybils via a living trellis of mutual attestations: each action needs countersigns from established peers. Newcomers expand their trellis only after original work, such as a coherent sonnet on shared history. An attacker creating many fakes must bribe or compromise real agents for every identity, or accept slow organic growth. A sudden comet of new identities is flagged by the mesh, making mass Sybil creation costly in social capital and time.
